paragraphs.title: The Promise of Protection and Descendants

easy.question: What does the Lord promise Abram at the beginning of the passage?
answers: To protect him and give him a great reward
To give him a new land
To make him a king
easy.explanation: The Lord says, “I am thy shield, and thy exceeding great reward.”

easy.question: What is Abram worried about?
answers: That he has no home
That he has no son to inherit from him
That he does not have enough possessions
easy.explanation: Abram says that he is childless and fears that Eliezer, a member of his household, may become his heir.

easy.question: What does the Lord compare the number of Abram’s descendants to?
answers: The dust of the earth
The sand of the sea
The stars of heaven
easy.explanation: The Lord tells Abram to look toward heaven and count the stars, saying, “So shall thy seed be.”

medium.question: Why does Abram mention Eliezer as someone who might inherit from him?
answers: Because he has no son
Because Eliezer was a king
Because Eliezer was his brother
medium.explanation: Abram explains that he has not been given any offspring, so Eliezer, who was born in his household, might become his heir.

medium.question: In the sentence “I go childless,” what concern is Abram expressing?
answers: That he is very wealthy
That he has no children or descendants
That he is traveling far away
medium.explanation: The surrounding verses make clear that Abram is concerned because he has no son or descendant.

medium.question: What does the Lord tell Abram after Abram mentions Eliezer as his heir?
answers: Eliezer will indeed be his heir
Abram will have no heir at all
The one who comes from Abram’s own body will be his heir
medium.explanation: The Lord corrects Abram’s fear, saying that the one who comes from his own bowels will be his heir.

challenge.question: What detail in the verses shows that Eliezer is not Abram’s son?
answers: He is described as one born in Abram’s house, not as Abram’s son
He is mentioned as a star
He goes with Abram into the heavens
challenge.explanation: Abram describes Eliezer as someone born in his household, rather than as a son born to him.

challenge.question: What does the statement “So shall thy seed be” show about the meaning of the stars?
answers: Abram’s descendants will live only at night
The number of his descendants will be enormous and difficult to count
Each descendant will literally be a star
challenge.explanation: The comparison with the stars emphasizes an extremely large number of descendants.

challenge.question: What happens in verse 6 after the Lord promises Abram many descendants?
answers: Abram leaves the land
Abram asks to appoint Eliezer
Abram believes in the Lord, and it is counted to him for righteousness
challenge.explanation: The verse says that Abram believed in the Lord, and the Lord counted it to him for righteousness.

questions.question: What detail in the verses shows that Eliezer is not Abram’s son?
answers: He is described as one born in Abram’s house, not as Abram’s son
He is mentioned as a star
He goes with Abram into the heavens
questions.explanation: Abram describes Eliezer as someone born in his household, rather than as a son born to him.

questions.question: What does the statement “So shall thy seed be” show about the meaning of the stars?
answers: Abram’s descendants will live only at night
The number of his descendants will be enormous and difficult to count
Each descendant will literally be a star
questions.explanation: The comparison with the stars emphasizes an extremely large number of descendants.

questions.question: What happens in verse 6 after the Lord promises Abram many descendants?
answers: Abram leaves the land
Abram asks to appoint Eliezer
Abram believes in the Lord, and it is counted to him for righteousness
questions.explanation: The verse says that Abram believed in the Lord, and the Lord counted it to him for righteousness.

paragraphs.title: The Promise of the Land and the Request for a Sign

easy.question: Who said to Abram, “I am the Lord”?
answers: The Lord
Abram
The king of Canaan
easy.explanation: The speaker in the verse is the Lord, who identifies himself to Abram.

easy.question: From where did the Lord bring Abram?
answers: Egypt
Ur of the Chaldees
Haran
easy.explanation: The Lord says that he brought Abram out of Ur of the Chaldees.

easy.question: What did the Lord promise to give Abram?
answers: Great wealth
Another son
This land
easy.explanation: The Lord says that he brought Abram out of Ur to give him this land to inherit.

medium.question: Why does the Lord mention bringing Abram out of Ur of the Chaldees?
answers: To remind Abram of what he had already done for him
To ask Abram to leave the land
To tell about a war
medium.explanation: The Lord recalls bringing Abram out of Ur to emphasize his past help and relationship with Abram.

medium.question: In the phrase “to give thee this land to inherit it,” what does “inherit” mean?
answers: To see the land
To pass through the land
To receive and possess the land
medium.explanation: In this context, inheriting the land means receiving it and possessing it as an inheritance.

medium.question: What did Abram do after the Lord promised to give him the land?
answers: He asked how he could know that he would inherit it
He immediately left the land
He said that he had already inherited it
medium.explanation: Abram asked, “Lord God, whereby shall I know that I shall inherit it?”

challenge.question: What connection between the two parts of the Lord’s statement stands out?
answers: The Lord describes Abram as someone he punished
The Lord recalls a past action and connects it with a future promise
The Lord cancels an earlier promise
challenge.explanation: The Lord recalls bringing Abram out of Ur in the past and connects that action with the promise of the land.

challenge.question: What can be understood from Abram’s question, “Whereby shall I know that I shall inherit it?”
answers: He is asking for certainty that the promise will be fulfilled
He claims that the land already belongs to him
He does not know who is speaking to him
challenge.explanation: Abram does not reject the Lord’s words; he asks how he can be certain that the promise will come true.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the Lord saying, “to give thee this land”?
answers: He is referring to a specific land under discussion
He is offering Abram any land he chooses
The land is unknown to everyone
challenge.explanation: The word “this” points to a particular land known in the context of the conversation.

questions.question: What connection between the two parts of the Lord’s statement stands out?
answers: The Lord describes Abram as someone he punished
The Lord recalls a past action and connects it with a future promise
The Lord cancels an earlier promise
questions.explanation: The Lord recalls bringing Abram out of Ur in the past and connects that action with the promise of the land.

questions.question: What can be understood from Abram’s question, “Whereby shall I know that I shall inherit it?”
answers: He is asking for certainty that the promise will be fulfilled
He claims that the land already belongs to him
He does not know who is speaking to him
questions.explanation: Abram does not reject the Lord’s words; he asks how he can be certain that the promise will come true.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the Lord saying, “to give thee this land”?
answers: He is referring to a specific land under discussion
He is offering Abram any land he chooses
The land is unknown to everyone
questions.explanation: The word “this” points to a particular land known in the context of the conversation.

paragraphs.title: The Covenant Ceremony and the Birds of Prey

easy.question: What did the Lord ask Abram to bring?
answers: Animals
Weapons
Bread and water
easy.explanation: The Lord asked Abram to bring a heifer, a she goat, a ram, a turtledove, and a young pigeon.

easy.question: What did Abram do to the larger animals?
answers: He released them
He divided them in two
He placed them on an altar
easy.explanation: Abram divided the animals in the midst, separating them into two parts.

easy.question: Which animal was not divided?
answers: The ram
The goat
The bird
easy.explanation: The verse specifically says that Abram did not divide the birds.

medium.question: What was the order of Abram’s actions?
answers: He took the animals, divided them, and laid the pieces opposite each other
He arranged the pieces, took the animals, and then divided them
He drove away the bird, took the animals, and then divided them
medium.explanation: Abram first took the animals, then divided them, and finally laid the pieces opposite each other.

medium.question: What does the phrase “a heifer of three years old” tell us?
answers: The heifer had three legs
The heifer was three years old
The heifer was divided into three pieces
medium.explanation: The phrase describes the animal’s age: it was three years old.

medium.question: What did Abram do when the birds came down on the carcasses?
answers: He gave them water
He took them home
He drove them away
medium.explanation: The verse says that Abram drove the birds away from the carcasses.

challenge.question: What was unusual about the way the bird was prepared compared with the other animals?
answers: The bird was not divided
The bird was given in three pieces
The bird was placed opposite itself
challenge.explanation: The other animals were divided and their pieces were placed opposite each other, but the bird was not divided.

challenge.question: What can be understood from the phrase “laid each piece one against another”?
answers: Abram joined all the pieces into one body
Abram placed each piece opposite its corresponding piece
Abram hid the pieces from the birds
challenge.explanation: The phrase describes arranging the pieces opposite each other, leaving a passage between them.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from Abram driving the birds away from the carcasses?
answers: He protected the animals and prepared them properly
He was afraid of all birds
He wanted to feed the birds
challenge.explanation: Driving the birds away shows that Abram guarded the carcasses and did not allow the birds to eat them.

questions.question: What was unusual about the way the bird was prepared compared with the other animals?
answers: The bird was not divided
The bird was given in three pieces
The bird was placed opposite itself
questions.explanation: The other animals were divided and their pieces were placed opposite each other, but the bird was not divided.

questions.question: What can be understood from the phrase “laid each piece one against another”?
answers: Abram joined all the pieces into one body
Abram placed each piece opposite its corresponding piece
Abram hid the pieces from the birds
questions.explanation: The phrase describes arranging the pieces opposite each other, leaving a passage between them.

questions.question: What can be inferred from Abram driving the birds away from the carcasses?
answers: He protected the animals and prepared them properly
He was afraid of all birds
He wanted to feed the birds
questions.explanation: Driving the birds away shows that Abram guarded the carcasses and did not allow the birds to eat them.

paragraphs.title: The Prophecy of Exile and Deliverance

easy.question: What fell upon Abram at the beginning of the passage?
answers: A deep sleep
Joy
A strong wind
easy.explanation: The verse says that a deep sleep fell upon Abram.

easy.question: For how long would Abram’s descendants be servants and afflicted?
answers: Forty years
Four hundred years
Four generations
easy.explanation: The prophecy says that they would serve and be afflicted for four hundred years.

easy.question: What would happen after the Lord judged the nation that enslaved Abram’s descendants?
answers: They would remain there
They would sleep in the wilderness
They would come out with great possessions
easy.explanation: The verse says that afterward they would come out with great substance.

medium.question: Why would the fourth generation return to the land?
answers: Because the iniquity of the Amorites would not yet be full
Because Abram requested it
Because they had no possessions
medium.explanation: The verse explains that the return would wait until the iniquity of the Amorites was full.

medium.question: In the phrase “thy seed shall be a stranger in a land that is not theirs,” what does “stranger” mean?
answers: A king in his own country
A foreign resident in a land that does not belong to him
A warrior in the wilderness
medium.explanation: The phrase describes someone living in a foreign land that is not his own.

medium.question: What was promised to Abram himself?
answers: That he would leave with great possessions
That he would conquer the land of the Amorites
That he would die in peace and be buried at a good old age
medium.explanation: The Lord told Abram that he would go to his fathers in peace and be buried in a good old age.

challenge.question: What is the order of events described in the prophecy?
answers: Slavery and affliction, judgment on the nation, departure with great possessions, return in the fourth generation
Departure with great possessions, slavery, judgment on the nation, immediate return
Return in the fourth generation, slavery, departure with great possessions, judgment on the nation
challenge.explanation: The passage describes slavery and affliction first, then judgment, followed by departure with possessions and a later return.

challenge.question: What is the main contrast between Abram’s fate and the fate of his descendants?
answers: Abram will remain in the land, while his descendants will conquer many lands
Abram will die in peace, while his descendants will experience slavery and affliction
Abram will leave with great possessions, while his descendants will be buried at a good old age
challenge.explanation: Abram is promised a peaceful death and old age, while his descendants will experience exile, slavery, and affliction.

challenge.question: In this context, what does “thou shalt go to thy fathers” mean?
answers: Abram will move in with his family
Abram will visit his ancestors
Abram will die and join his ancestors
challenge.explanation: This is a respectful expression for death, as confirmed by the promise that Abram will be buried in a good old age.

questions.question: What is the order of events described in the prophecy?
answers: Slavery and affliction, judgment on the nation, departure with great possessions, return in the fourth generation
Departure with great possessions, slavery, judgment on the nation, immediate return
Return in the fourth generation, slavery, departure with great possessions, judgment on the nation
questions.explanation: The passage describes slavery and affliction first, then judgment, followed by departure with possessions and a later return.

answers: Abram will remain in the land, while his descendants will conquer many lands

Abram will leave with great possessions, while his descendants will be buried at a good old age
questions.explanation: Abram is promised a peaceful death and old age, while his descendants will experience exile, slavery, and affliction.

answers: Abram will move in with his family

Abram will die and join his ancestors
questions.explanation: This is a respectful expression for death, as confirmed by the promise that Abram will be buried in a good old age.

paragraphs.title: The Fire Passing Between the Pieces

easy.question: What happened to the sun at the beginning of verse 17?
answers: It went down
It rose
It disappeared in the morning
easy.explanation: The verse says that the sun went down.

easy.question: What passed between the pieces?
answers: A cloud and rain
A smoking furnace and a burning lamp
Abraham and Sarah
easy.explanation: The verse describes a smoking furnace and a burning lamp passing between the pieces.

easy.question: What did the Lord give Abram in the covenant?
answers: This land to his descendants
All the animals
Only the river of Egypt
easy.explanation: The Lord said, “Unto thy seed have I given this land.”

medium.question: What does the phrase “a deep darkness” describe in the passage?
answers: Heavy darkness
A strong wind
Bright light
medium.explanation: The passage describes the darkness that came after the sun went down.

medium.question: What happened first, and what happened afterward?
answers: The covenant was made, and then the sun went down
The sun went down and it became dark, and then the covenant was made
The Euphrates River was formed, and then the lamp appeared
medium.explanation: The sun went down and darkness came in verse 17; verse 18 then says that the Lord made the covenant.

medium.question: Why are the two rivers mentioned in verse 18?
answers: To describe the boundaries of the promised land
To tell where Abram lived
To describe the location of the pieces
medium.explanation: The rivers mark the boundaries of the land given to Abram’s descendants, from the river of Egypt to the Euphrates.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the furnace and lamp passing between the pieces?
answers: The animals escaped
An event connected with making the covenant took place
It was time to begin a journey
challenge.explanation: The objects pass between the pieces immediately before the covenant is announced, so the act is connected with the covenant ceremony.

challenge.question: Which detail emphasizes that the promise was given to Abram’s future descendants, not only to Abram?
answers: The words “in the same day”
The words “the river Euphrates”
The words “unto thy seed have I given”
challenge.explanation: The words “unto thy seed” make clear that the promise concerns Abram’s descendants.

challenge.question: What kind of boundary description is used in the phrase “from the river of Egypt unto the great river, the river Euphrates”?
answers: The land is described as stretching from west to east
The land includes only a small area around Jerusalem
The land lies entirely inside one river
challenge.explanation: The verse names one boundary at the beginning and another at the end, describing a broad stretch of territory.

answers: The animals escaped

questions.explanation: The objects pass between the pieces immediately before the covenant is announced, so the act is connected with the covenant ceremony.

paragraphs.title: The Boundaries of the Land and the Peoples of Canaan

easy.question: Which people are mentioned first in the verses?
answers: The Kenites
The Hittites
The Amorites
easy.explanation: The Kenites are listed first, at the beginning of verse 19.

easy.question: How many peoples are mentioned in verse 20?
answers: Two
Three
Four
easy.explanation: Verse 20 mentions the Hittites, the Perizzites, and the Rephaims—three peoples.

easy.question: Which people are listed last?
answers: The Girgashites
The Canaanites
The Jebusites
easy.explanation: The Jebusites appear last, at the end of verse 21.

medium.question: Which people are mentioned immediately after the Hittites?
answers: The Perizzites
The Rephaims
The Amorites
medium.explanation: The list reads: the Hittites, the Perizzites, and then the Rephaims.

medium.question: How many peoples are mentioned in verse 21?
answers: Three
Four
Five
medium.explanation: Verse 21 mentions the Amorites, Canaanites, Girgashites, and Jebusites—four peoples.

medium.question: What are the Rephaims in the phrase “and the Rephaims”?
answers: Rivers
Kings
A people or group of people
medium.explanation: The name appears in a list of peoples and groups, so it refers here to a people or group.

challenge.question: How many peoples are mentioned altogether in verses 19–21?
answers: Ten
Nine
Eleven
challenge.explanation: Verse 19 lists three names, verse 20 lists three, and verse 21 lists four, for a total of ten.

challenge.question: Which people are third in the list in verse 21?
answers: The Canaanites
The Girgashites
The Jebusites
challenge.explanation: The order is the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Girgashites, and the Jebusites.

challenge.question: What idea is shared by all three verses?
answers: A journey through different lands
A war between peoples
A list of peoples or groups
challenge.explanation: The verses do not describe events; they list various peoples and groups in succession.
